title: India in New Zealand: Kohli Needs Four Runs to Reach 600 as ODI Series Opens Wednesday
excerpt: Kohli's 596 ODI runs in New Zealand leave him two behind Sehwag and chasing Tendulkar's 821, as India return for five ODIs after losing the home series to the Black Caps in January.
body:
• India's five-match ODI series in New Zealand opens on Wednesday, November 4, at Eden Park in Auckland.
  • Virat Kohli has 596 ODI runs in New Zealand at an average of 49.66; he needs four more for 600 and sits just two behind Virender Sehwag's 598.
  • Sachin Tendulkar holds the record for most ODI runs by an Indian in New Zealand, with 821; Kohli's 123 at Napier in 2014 is his highest score there.
  • New Zealand won the teams' last ODI series 2-1 in India in January 2026, its first bilateral ODI series win on Indian soil.

India begin a five-match ODI series in New Zealand on Wednesday at Eden Park, and the record book for this fixture has a live thread running through it: Virat Kohli is four runs short of 600 ODI runs on New Zealand soil, and two runs behind the man in second place on India's all-time list there.

The numbers Kohli carries into Auckland

In 13 ODIs in New Zealand, Kohli has scored 596 runs at an average of 49.66, with one century and four half-centuries. The century is his standout innings in the country: 123 off 111 balls at Napier on January 19, 2014, still his highest ODI score in New Zealand, followed on that tour by 78 off 65 at Hamilton. Ahead of him on India's in-New-Zealand run list sit only Virender Sehwag, with 598 runs in 12 matches, and Sachin Tendulkar, whose 821 runs remain the benchmark for an Indian batter in New Zealand. Kohli passes Sehwag with three runs and reaches 600 with four; Tendulkar's mark is out of reach for this series alone.

Form against this opponent

Kohli's overall record against New Zealand, home and away, is stronger still: 1,897 runs in 36 ODIs at an average of 57.48, including 240 runs in three matches in the January 2026 series in India, among them 124 off 108 balls. That series, though, went New Zealand's way, 2-1, the Black Caps' first bilateral ODI series victory on Indian soil, which is what gives this return series its edge: India are playing in conditions where their recent record is thinner than their home dominance suggests.

What to watch in the series

The milestones are the early subplot. One innings of any substance moves Kohli past Sehwag into second place on the in-New-Zealand list, and the five-match format gives him repeated chances at the 600 mark at venues where he has scored before. The larger question is the one January raised: whether India can convert their batting depth into results away from home. New Zealand, meanwhile, have lost Rachin Ravindra and Mark Chapman to injury ahead of the series. The series opener is at Eden Park on Wednesday, November 4.
